en: An |Efficient| ability refunds 1 |CORE POWER| at the end of any scene in which it was used, so it is available again in the next one.

"Some manufactures ask stupid questions such as "how much heat can this frame take before permanent damage to the structural integrity of the chassis?" or "how do we make the invasive code properly avoid the countermeasures of a witch class mech?". Well fuck them because we ask the real questions, like "how many guns can we put on one guy?" and "how heavy of a tungsten ball can we shoot at high enough velocity to kill 10 men in a row?". Then we take those answers, turn them into cannons, slap em' on a prototype and BAM! good to GO. Fuck you Harrison eat shit this is real science."

- recovered log from fired IPS-N R&D worker

The Fitzgerald is not named for some daring brigand, terror of the high seas, or fearless rebel fighting against impossible odds. It is named after a tragedy, because for the longest time, that's all the Fitzgerald ever was. Originally a casualty of corporate reorganization and mismanagement, it bounced between team after team, each one being disbanded for one reason or another. Eventually, it was relegated to the lowest tier of development. Being sent to work on it was almost synonymous for being fired. And yet, after decades of rotting away as IPS-N's reject pile, the unthinkable happened. It was complete. To this day it stands as a testament to hard work, persevering and toiling away at thankless labor for the slightest chance at glory. Those who choose to pilot the Fitzgerald embody this, because it doesn't matter how many times you've been knocked down, how often you get turned into a heap of slag, or exploded into shrapnel. What matters is that you have a cannon nearly as big as you are, and there is nowhere for them to hide.

One of the earliest prototypes for mechanized combat the M/K2 heralds from a time before the integration of ammo feeds and every weapon needed to be manually reloaded. Because of this, the frame was entirely focused around trying to get around this major limitation through jury-rigged hybridized reloads or just straight up swapping to a new gun. This approach was ultimately a failure, however, as there was simply no way to deal with the high temperatures and the fragility of the O.R.S replenishment system. GMS scrapped the project entirely to focus on more reliable alternatives as was befitting their brand. The M/K2 was later rediscovered by janitorial staff during an archival purge and was spread on the Omninet among enthusiasts. Some brave pilots even choose to take updated versions into battle, trying to make use of its unique abilities with a modern arsenal.
The Fitzgerald receives |+1 Difficulty| on all SYSTEMS saves and checks.

The BIZARRE CANNON is built through the Fitzgerald's chassis rather than mounted on it: it occupies no weapon mount and cannot take a weapon mod. Its active MORE BLACK POWDER protocol grants the cannon a second profile.
On attack: you take 2 |AP| kinetic damage and are knocked back 2 spaces, away from the direction of fire.
For the rest of this scene, the BIZARRE CANNON gains the following profile: Heavy Cannon, |AP|, |Reliable 3|, |Heat 1| (Self). [|Line 15|] [2d6 kinetic + 1d6 explosive damage]
On attack: you take 3 |AP| kinetic damage and are knocked back 3 spaces, in any direction. On hit: targets must succeed on a |hull save| or become |prone|.
The BIZARRE CANNON has a second, heavier profile for the rest of this scene.
The Fitzgerald may ignore line of sight when attacking with |cannon| or |Line| weapons. Targets attacked this way have |soft cover|.
Attacked without being seen: the shot treats this target as having soft cover.
1/round, when the Fitzgerald critically hits a character with a |cannon|, that character must make a |hull save| or be knocked |Prone|.
306 lb. of tungsten will fix most problems.
You can fire this cannon three times before it needs to be reloaded. You may choose to fire all three shots at once by using the Grapeshot profile.
Fire one of the gun's three rounds.
Firing all three of its munitions at once, the gun must be reloaded before it is shot again. On hit: target must make a |hull save| or be |Shredded| until the end of your next turn.
HIGH EXPLOSIVE ANTI EVERYTHING ROUNDS as they have been called, are crammed full of as much explosive power as possible, leading to devastating, if unreliable, results.

Whenever you destroy a hostile character or deployable with a |rifle|, |launcher|, or |cannon| you may expend a charge to make them explode violently. All characters within |Burst 1| of the destroyed character or deployable must make an |Agility save| or take 1d6+1 |AP| kinetic damage.

1/round, when the Fitzgerald makes a successful ranged attack with a |Line| weapon, it may deal an additional +1 bonus damage to the next character hit within that line, increasing on consecutive hits.

Originally based on the Nelson's iconic Ramjet technology, the Hull-break Thrusters take it in a new direction. Control and survivability are thrown out the window to focus on pure power. Why go around someone when you can go straight through them?

Expend a charge: you fly your |Speed| in a straight line in any direction, moving through hostile characters. All hostile characters you pass through or become adjacent with during this movement, must make a |hull save| or be knocked |Prone| and take 3 |AP| kinetic damage. For each occupied space you pass through, you take 1 |AP| kinetic damage. This movement ignores |engagement| and does not provoke reactions.

A masterwork of design built to devastate any target with heavy armor. A solid tungsten shell is applied to all munitions and their inner casings are filled with a shaped warhead charge. Unfortunately, due to the specific conditions needed to trigger the activation of the warhead, RIPPER rounds provide no significant advantage against non-armored targets.
This weapon deals +1d6 bonus damage against targets with at least 1 Armor. Attacks made with this weapon lose |AP| and cannot gain |AP| by any means.

The Carronade functions on a simple principle: there is no such thing as cover from a wrecking ball. So, IPS-N made that wrecking ball, packed it into a cannon, and leased it out to those discerning individuals who understand the true spirit of hard working hunks of metal moving very quickly.
This weapon ignores cover and deals 10 |AP| kinetic damage to all objects or terrain within the line.
This weapon ignores cover and deals 10 |AP| kinetic damage to all objects or terrain within the line.

Originally meant to quickly patch hull breaches, the Grit Latch Magnets are a uniquely ISP-N innovation. Consisting of a fine metal grit packed tightly into a sphere, upon activation the grit explodes outwards into a cloud, where it magnetically attaches to all nearby metal. Tiny thermal charges bound to the granules then quickly burn, melting it into a slag almost instantaneously. The result is an effective, if temporary, layer of armature.
Spend a charge and choose a |Blast 1| area within |Sensors|. All characters within the area gain 1 armor until the end of your next turn.
Plated in grit latch magnets: 1 armor until the end of the Fitzgerald's next turn.
1/scene the M/K2 may ignore the |Ordnance| tag until the end of the current turn.
Ignore the |Ordnance| tag until the end of this turn.
|Ordnance| weapons may be fired this turn after moving or acting.
Gain +1 |Accuracy| on the first attack you make with a |Loading| weapon that is not |Superheavy| on your turn.
The M/K2's O.R.S replenishment system can be forced to run hot, feeding every |Loading| weapon on the chassis at the cost of waste heat.
For the rest of the scene, you ignore the |Loading| property of your weapons but gain 1d3 |heat| each time you fire a |Loading| weapon.
|Loading| weapons do not need reloading, but each firing costs 1d3 |heat|.

The Barbarossa has offers a simple choice: you kill it and get swarmed by its friends, or you don't kill it and you get the business end of a ship-class spool weapon. With the start of the broadcasts, Harrison Armory decided to take this principle to the next level; why even let them have the choice? The Subutai is the next step, armed with the experimental diversion rail, it locks down the battlefield leaving a trail of destruction in its wake. Now sure, you can't annihilate a bunker from a ridge over, but it's the price you pay for unparalleled defensive artillery. At the end of the day, you are still a solid block of metal, and ain't nothing gonna stand in your way.
The Subutai reduces all |Kinetic| and |Explosive| damage by 1 before |Armor| and |Resistances=lancer.term.resistance| are calculated.

1/round, as a |free action| at the end of its turn, the Subutai may move up to 3 spaces ignoring terrain and |Immobilized|. It must move in a straight line directly towards an allied character within |line of sight|. It may only take this action if it is |Immobilized|.
Move up to 3 spaces in a straight line directly towards an allied character within |line of sight|, ignoring terrain and |Immobilized|.

And God said, Let there be light: and there was light. And Harrison said, Let there be 73-pound hyperdense tungsten bars gravitationally launched at 128 meters per second that infect their target with forced system lock: and there was 73-pound hyperdense tungsten bars gravitationally launched at 128 meters per second that infect their target with forced system lock. God is dead and we have killed her!

The DIVERSION RAIL is built through the Subutai's chassis rather than mounted on it: it occupies no weapon mount and cannot take a weapon mod. Its active GATHER ROUND protocol grants the DRAW FIRE reaction for the rest of the scene.
For the rest of the scene, you gain the Draw Fire reaction.
For the rest of the scene, you gain the Draw Fire reaction.
On attack: You become |immobilized| until the start of your next turn. On hit: The target takes |+2 difficulty| on all attacks that do not target the Subutai until the end of their next turn.
The target takes |+2 difficulty| on all attacks that do not target the Subutai until the end of their next turn.
A hostile character within |Range| of the Diversion Rail and |line of sight| makes a |ranged attack| against an allied character within |Sensors|.
The attack is made against you instead. After the attack, you may make an attack against the hostile character with the Diversion Rail.

Horus pattern groups have always been a contentious subject, the lines between one group and another can be blurry and heated debates about them are a common sight on the omninet. Originally, the Myconid was thought to be an offshoot of the Balor, its form comprised of thousands of tiny nanites shifting and rippling like water. However, after the official designation of greenwash, the Myconid began to be more clearly differentiated due to its more benevolent properties. Unlike other types of nanites, greenwash is incapable of tearing apart material and can not replicate itself, working only to surround and protect its designated targets. These less aggressive properties have led many to misunderstand the Myconid, thinking it a kindness compared to its siblings. They could not be more wrong. It is myriad, a shambling mound of churning wash, an angel emitting halos of shimmering nanite spores, a machine of propagation and rot. To those who endanger the network, it is nightmare made material.
1/round, the Myconid may use a |reaction| an additional time. This cannot be used on |reactions| that are 1/scene or 1/mission.
{unit} cannot spend the Symbiosis reaction on a 1/scene or 1/mission reaction.
1/round, when the Myconid takes damage, an allied character within |Sensors| gains |OVERSHIELD| equal to |GRIT|.

The Myconid releases a cloud of nanite spores around itself. For the rest of the scene all adjacent allies gain immunity to |Impaired| and have |+1 armor|. Hostile characters within |burst 2| of the Myconid are |Slowed| and |Impaired|.
|Slowed| and |Impaired| while within |burst 2| of the Myconid.
A cloud of nanite spores surrounds the Myconid.
Gain the Uffish Gyre reaction, which is the only way you can attack with this weapon.
An allied character within |threat| starts to move. This does not require |line of sight| or a clear path between you and the target.

Make a melee attack against evasion 8, on hit the allied character gains +2 armor until the start of their next turn. This doesn’t count against the maximum number of |reactions| you can make in a turn.
|+2 armor| until the start of your next turn.

The Mourning Cloak was a triumph of design, a masterpiece of ideas folded and sculpted together into a perfect gestalt. But even perfection can be improved at Smith-Shimano. Every piece can be broken down and improved, each moving part can become its own triumph. And when these parts are put together, you can get something even stranger and more beautiful than before. Or you could get the Maidens Blush, a bastardized, overly designed, paracausal patchwork of ideas. This is of course not to say that it is not an effective frame, or even a bad one, merely that it stands against the typical design philosophies of SSC. It reached licensing to push the boundaries of what SSC can make possible. It does not build upon the Firmament-manipulation groundwork laid by its predecessor, it eschewed years of work to rely upon strange technology. All to prove that even the strangest ideas can be made manifest. It stands as a reminder that there is no such thing as more perfect, it is all just different facets of the same idea, and one day, that SSC will see the whole for what it truly may be.
1/round, whenever the Maiden's Blush critically hits with a |melee| weapon, the target must make a |Hull save|. On a failure, they become |Impaired| and |Slowed| until the end of their next turn.
1/round if the Maiden's Blush would |teleport|, it instead may become |Invisible| until the beginning of its next turn. It immediately loses |Invisible| if it takes damage.
1/round if the Maiden's Blush would |teleport|, it instead may become |Invisible| until the beginning of its next turn. It immediately loses |Invisible| if it takes damage.
{unit} fades from view; {source} does not happen.
There is nowhere to fold into. Become Invisible instead, and spend the Uncertainty Field for this round?
The fold is called off. Become Invisible instead, and spend the Uncertainty Field for this round?
{unit} finds nowhere to fold, and fades from view instead.
{unit} calls off the fold, and fades from view instead.
{unit} took damage and is no longer Invisible.
If the Maiden's Blush begins its turn |Invisible|, it may reroll its first |melee| attack roll it makes on that turn. It must keep the second result.
The first |melee| attack roll this turn may be rerolled, keeping the second result.

Roll 2d6. You |teleport| to a free space within a Range equal to what you rolled, without requiring line of sight. Characters adjacent to the space you teleport to must make a |Systems save| or treat you as |Invisible| until the end of the scene. If you roll two 1s you teleport to a space of the GM's choice. This teleportation cannot be prevented. This ability is |Efficient| and will refund 1 Core Point at the end of any scene in which this ability was used.
{unit} rolled two 1s: the fold lands where the firmament chooses.
{unit} is boxed in: the fold finds nowhere to land.
Treats the Maiden's Blush as |Invisible| for the rest of the scene.
A hostile character within sensors misses you with an attack.

Roll 1d6: You may |teleport| up to that many spaces in the direction of the attacker. If this puts the attacker in |Threat| of one of your weapons, you may immediately use that weapon to |Skirmish| against them.
{unit} finds no space to fold into.

The earth was made to be shattered, metal was made to be heated and broken and battered. The world was made to be destroyed piece by piece. The Vauban stands as the Harrison's testament to dominion, each piece bent towards the singular point of progress and control. With the vast amount of data being spewed out of the Broadcasts it was only a matter of time until something truly devastating was unleashed that really ought to have stayed unknown. The Vauban was built upon that something. Gravity control is a tough nut to crack, and even now its secrets are not yet all teased out of its potential, but HA found enough to work with, and work with it they did. By leveraging hyper localized gravity pulses, the Vauban can sunder the ground, turning it into a mass of dangerous shards that can rend and drag down unwary opponents. No one can beat gravity forever.
A hostile character within Sensors and |line of sight| becomes |Slowed| or |Immobilized|.
They take 1d6 |Kinetic| damage and become |impaired| until the end of their next turn.

When a hostile character within sensors and |line of sight| enters, or starts their turn, in an area of |difficult terrain|, they must make a |Hull save| or become |Slowed| until the end of their next turn. A character that succeeds this save is unaffected by Sap until the end of their next turn.

When a hostile character within sensors and |line of sight| enters, or starts their turn, in an area of |difficult terrain|, they must make a |Hull save| or become |Slowed| until the end of their next turn. A character that succeeds this save is unaffected by Sap until the end of their next turn.
While the Vauban is in at least one space of |difficult terrain|, all ranged and melee attacks made against it have +1 |difficulty|. Any adjacent allied mechs also benefit from this ability.

For the rest of the scene, you gain the following benefits: The Vauban generates a |Burst 1| field of |difficult terrain|. Saves you force are made with +1 Difficulty. When a hostile character fails a save you forced, they take 3 |AP| |Kinetic| damage. Each character can be affected by this ability only once per round.
Saves forced by the Vauban are made with +1 |difficulty|.
Choose a |Blast 1| area within Sensors and |line of sight| that contains no hostile Characters. For the rest of the scene it becomes |difficult terrain|.

The Primrose is the flagship model of SSC's LIM-AMOK line, and the culmination of SSC's experimentations with Broadcast tech. Built to be a close range combatant, with significant evasive and diversion options, it excels with elegant melee combat while offering variable engagement distance options. It marks SSC's first foray into large scale hand-to-hand options with rapid limb extension and magnetic attachment points allowing massive weapons to be hefted around with ease. Its ability to quickly close the distance, control a wide area around it, and evade any retaliation, has made it a popular option for many pilots who prefer direct and efficient solutions, immaculately done.
1/round, when the Primrose critically hits with a |Heavy| or |Superheavy| melee weapon, the target must succeed a |Hull save| or be knocked |Prone|.
|Heavy| and |Superheavy| melee weapons on the Primrose gain +1 |threat|.

The details and technological foundation of the Möbian Rainbow is a closely guarded secret within Exotic Materials. What is known however, is that it acts as a perpetual coating that forms a thin transparent layer overtop of mechs, creating a kaleidoscopic effect. The combat benefits of this coating remain unknown, but reports indicate a significant increase in successful operations while it is applied.
Each time a hostile character fails an attack against you, gain +1 |EVASION| for the rest of the scene up to a maximum of +3.
+{bonus} |EVASION| for the rest of the scene, one for each hostile attack that has failed against you.

For the rest of the scene you gain one of the following effects:
Wormhole Grasp
Your weapons gain +1 |threat| and you may |Overwatch| with |Superheavy| weapons. Attacks made this way deal half damage, |Heat|, and |Burn|. 1/round, when you damage a character with an |Overwatch|, they must succeed a |Hull save| or be |Slowed| until the end of their next turn.
Shimmering Shield
While you are in |cover|, melee attacks against you receive |+1 Difficulty|. Additionally, Effervescent Immunity can stack up to a maximum of +5. If it would increase past this point, you instead gain 1d3 |OVERSHIELD|.

Your weapons gain +1 |threat| and you may |Overwatch| with |Superheavy| weapons. Attacks made this way deal half damage, |Heat|, and |Burn|. 1/round, when you damage a character with an |Overwatch|, they must succeed a |Hull save| or be |Slowed| until the end of their next turn.

While you are in |cover|, melee attacks against you receive |+1 Difficulty|. Additionally, Effervescent Immunity can stack up to a maximum of +5. If it would increase past this point, you instead gain 1d3 |OVERSHIELD|.

One of SSC's more experimental creations, the Rend Axe is a masterwork of design. Consisting of a ferromagnetic blade and a focused propulsion system, it allows for quick strikes that can puncture through armor and peel it away.

You may attack with this weapon without expending or requiring charges, and this weapon can be destroyed (due to critical damage or other effects) even if it has no charges remaining. On a |critical hit|, until the start of their next turn, the target is |Shredded|.
1/round, you may expend a charge to attack with this weapon as a |free action| during your turn.

While its name does not bely its true purpose, the Dazzling Wind suite of systems is nevertheless a core part of SSC's LIM-AMOK line. Powerful hydraulic mobility augments allow for a pilot to leap across a battlefield, easily clearing any terrain or hostile forces. Unfortunately for its users however, each time it is recharged, it must be manually put back together in a painstakingly long process to achieve maximum combat efficiency.
Expend a charge: fly your |Speed| in a straight line. At the end of your movement, you may choose a hostile character adjacent to you; they must make a |hull save| or be knocked |Prone|.

SSC does not acknowledge the common term for weapons such as the Acrasial Falcata. It is uncouth, a violent misrepresentation of the mastery of its design. A long elegant blade, fashioned in the style of ancient Cradle. A flash-printer ammunition feed contained within the handle. The small cannon in the cross-guard, the perfect response to a would-be assailant. The Falcata is no mere "gunsword", it is far too sharp, too clever, and too wonderous to be contained by such a term.
A hostile character within |line of sight| attempts to hit you with a melee attack.
The attack is made with |+1 Difficulty|. If the attack misses, the attacker takes 3 |AP| |Kinetic| damage and must succeed a |Hull save| or be knocked |prone|.

A specialty modification for melee combatants, the DDMR, or Debris Detachment Magnetic Aegis, adds some additional heft and reach its attached weapon. Its primary function however lies in its ferrofluid core, upon impact with a target, any debris are pulled back towards the user and suspended in the air around them. The field of particles are able to absorb stray blows and offer the user some additional safety while up close and personal. [>//:why is it called DDMR if the last letter stands for Aegis? [>//:shut up //<]
This weapon gains |+1 Threat|. 1/round, on a hit with the weapon this mod is applied to, the next attack against you has |+1 Difficulty| until the start of your next turn.
The next attack against you has |+1 Difficulty|.

Meant to be one of the centerpieces of the LIM-AMOK line, the Eternity Hammer is the counterpart to the complex designs that surround it. There is elegance too in simplicity. There is only so much sheer force any structure can handle. There are only so many types of shielding available to a foe. There are only so many times a pilot can miss. When you have biggest and best hammer there is, the whole world starts to look like a nail.
On hit: hostile characters adjacent to the target must make an |Agility save| or take 2 |Burn|.
